analyst.summary: HCL Technologies delivered a solid Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) on profit and margins - net profit up 20% YoY to Rs 4,624 crore, with margins improving - and logged its highest-ever first-quarter deal bookings of $2.4 billion. But underlying dollar revenue growth was just 2.6-3% year-on-year and actually shrank slightly versus the prior quarter, management kept its already-modest full-year growth guidance of 1-4% unchanged, and the company's higher-margin software business shrank 5.3% with a meaningful margin hit. Management also flagged that AI-driven pricing pressure is trimming 2-3% off its existing business, an effect it hopes new AI-related work will offset but hasn't yet proven out, and it committed roughly Rs 3,500 crore to build its own AI data centres - a departure from its traditionally asset-light, high-payout model, with no disclosed payback timeline. At about 18 times earnings - near the stock's own long-term average - the market isn't overpaying for growth it may not get, but nor is the stock cheap enough to look like a clear opportunity given the real, company-specific soft spots layered on top of an industry-wide slowdown in growth guidance. We rate it a Hold: a well-run, well-capitalised, dividend-paying business going through a genuine growth air-pocket, not a name we'd add to or exit from at current levels.
